chapter: Arnold DePass's life and the Cadillac years
title: Cadillac and fairgrounds: Arnold's drumming and Manuel Perez's Imperial band
summary: Uncle Dave and Jimmy Newman at the Cadillac, the Armistead brass band and young Olympians at the fairgrounds, her husband's drum rolls, and Manuel Perez and the Imperial.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: It'll come to me. Well, he used to play piano there at Cadillac. My Uncle played, uh, uh, Uncle Dave sometime used to play, Dave Depass used to play clarinet. Well, that's my husband's brother. He used to play sometime with your Daddy, you know. Jimmy Newman was playing there also one time at the Cadillac. Until he went away and we had that cook auction with him. And, uh, they used to play at the fairgrounds, you see. They had the Armist brass band at the fairgrounds. And they had the young Olympians who were supposed to be at a jazz band, you know, play all that bratty music that's fast stuff, you know. And the nice people would dance by the Armist brass band. You'd have to do that skipping dance, you know, like waltzing around and all that. But your Daddy would play it in other words, what they called the Tunk. They'd play out there. And, uh, sometimes, like, my friend and I, we'd go looking around and your Daddy would say, Don't come here, baby. Get away from here. You know, it wasn't for the nice people. For the rough and ready ones. They'd play that. Your Daddy would have that hat on and the uniform, you know. And he used to wear, like, suspenders, you know. And when you get real warm there and beating that drum, he'd put one of them suspenders down, you know. One of the suspenders down and he'd have that cap on the side. And I'm telling you, he really could beat that drum, too. Could make one of the best, how do you call that, rolls on the drum, you know. A lot of people say he really had a gift to that, you know. He played by air, too, but he really had a gift to it. Because often, different people say you'd never think that, you know, that he played. And he had so many opportunities to go away, but he never would accept it. Because I never would want to go away. I always wanted to stay, you know. And he always wanted to say, come on, let's sell out and go away. And when Manuel Perez went away, still a long time, you know. You know Manuel Perez, the trumpet player. Well, then after a number of years, he came, stood here and laid down and died there. He had a son. Is his son still playing?
I've never heard of his son.
That's funny, I didn't know about that.

He had a son who was trying to follow his footstep. I don't know if he ever kept it up, you know. Well, he was a fine musician, you know. He was, Manuel Perez also was with, one time, they had, let's see, what was the name of his band? The Superior? I think the old one. Manuel Perez? The old one. Was it the Superior?
No, that was Billy Morrero's band. Billy Moran's band. The Imperial, yes. It must have been the Onward band, you think?

No, the Imperial, yeah. Imperial, that was his dance band. Yeah, he had the Imperial, that's right. That was his dance band. The Onward was a brass band. I knew it was something about, he had the Imperial. Cause, and sometime he played with Papa Sellers, then. Sometime, you know, cause they both were trumpet players, but sometime, yeah, I played with them.
